items.title: Four Motives for a Trainee to Cultivate Deep Concentration, and Karma Reduced to Just Four Colours

items.zh: 又有四種學增上心方便。謂未離欲者，為得不還果，或不還果，依未至定求現法樂住；又為令他斷諸惡法，及往善趣；又為自己斷諸煩惱，得勝決擇。又有二業四相差別。謂轉所攝業差別有三，還所攝業總立一種。當知初業，一向能感不可愛果惡趣異熟；第二業、一向能感可愛樂果色無色界異熟；第三業、能感愛非愛果欲界天人異熟；第四業、能斷前三業。
items.en: There are also four means by which a trainee cultivates the higher mind: one not yet free of desire does so in order to attain the fruit of non-return; or, having attained non-return, one relies on threshold concentration seeking the ease of the present life; or one does so in order to lead others to sever unwholesome states and reach a favourable destiny; or one does so in order to sever one's own afflictions and attain superior discernment. There are also two kinds of karma with four distinguishing marks: three belong to the class comprised within flux, and the class comprised within return is established as a single kind. Know that the first kind of karma uniformly ripens into the disagreeable fruit of the evil destinies; the second uniformly ripens into the agreeable fruit of existence in the form or formless realm; the third ripens into a mixed fruit, agreeable or disagreeable, in the desire realm among gods and humans; the fourth is able to sever all three of the preceding kinds.

items.title: Pleasure and Benefit in Four Combinations, and the Four Yokes That Bind Beings to Suffering

items.zh: 又有四種諸有情類增上勤務。一、樂而非利益，二、利益而非樂，三、亦樂亦利益，四、非樂非利益。又有四門起諸煩惱，能令有情與生等苦和合不離。一、染著諸欲門，二、染著色無色等至門，三、外道諸見門，四、住此法中未得眼者無智門。又修聖道，令此四門所生眾苦速得離繫。如能令有情與苦和合，能令順流取後有業難可解脫，當知亦爾。
items.en: There are also four kinds of diligent striving among sentient beings: first, pleasant but not beneficial; second, beneficial but not pleasant; third, both pleasant and beneficial; fourth, neither pleasant nor beneficial. There are also four gateways giving rise to affliction, which cause sentient beings to remain bound together with the suffering of birth and the rest: first, the gateway of attachment to sensory desires; second, the gateway of attachment to the attainments of the form and formless realms; third, the gateway of non-Buddhist views; fourth, the gateway of ignorance in one who, though dwelling within this very teaching, has not yet attained the eye [of wisdom]. By cultivating the noble path, the multitude of sufferings born from these four gateways are swiftly released from their bondage. As these cause sentient beings to remain bound together with suffering, know it is likewise so that they cause the karma that grasps at further existence, following the stream, to be difficult to escape.

items.title: One Being, Sorted Four Different Ways: By Bondage, By Precepts and View, By Birth and Conduct, and By Who Actually Suffers

items.zh: 復有四種補特伽羅，當知遍攝一切補特伽羅。一者、異生，二者、未離欲有學，三者、已離欲有學，四者、超薩迦耶見一切無學。又有四種補特伽羅。一、自住律儀，不能為他宣說正法；二、自不住律儀，而能為他宣說正法；三、俱能作；四、俱不能作。又有四種補特伽羅。一、族姓卑下，現行白法；二、族姓尊高、現行惡法；三、族姓卑下，現行惡法；四、族姓尊高，現行白法。此中最初，現法有苦，非於後法；第二、後法有苦，非於現法；第三、二世俱苦；第四、二世俱樂。又有四種補特伽羅。一、以苦自任不任於他而生非福。謂受外道自苦戒者。二、以苦任他不任於自而生非福，謂隨有一不律儀者。三、以苦俱任而生非福，謂諸國王及祠祀主馬祠祀等。四、不以苦任於自他而生大福，謂住靜慮者及離諸惡補特伽羅。
items.en: There are also four kinds of persons, comprehending all persons without exception: first, the ordinary being; second, the trainee not yet free of desire; third, the trainee already free of desire; fourth, the adept who has entirely transcended the view of a substantial self. There are also four kinds of persons: first, one who upholds precepts personally but cannot teach the true Dharma to others; second, one who does not personally uphold precepts but can teach the true Dharma to others; third, one who can do both; fourth, one who can do neither. There are also four kinds of persons: first, one who imposes suffering only on oneself and generates no merit thereby — one who undertakes a non-Buddhist ascetic's self-mortifying vows; second, one who imposes suffering only on others and generates no merit thereby — one who follows any unrestrained livelihood; third, one who imposes suffering on both self and others and generates no merit thereby — kings and those who preside over sacrificial rites such as the horse sacrifice; fourth, one who imposes suffering on neither self nor others and generates great merit thereby — one who dwells in meditative absorption and one who has abandoned all evil.

items.title: Four Faults of Speech, and the Four Marks of an Ordinary Person's Lie — the "Four Things" Category Closes

items.zh: 又略有四種語失。一、不實，二、乖離，三、毀德，四、無義。與此相違，當知即是四種語德。又略有四種非聖妄語。謂於見不見、顛倒而說。於聞不聞、於覺不覺、於知不知，當知亦爾。與此相違，當知即是賢聖諦語。
items.en: There are also, briefly, four faults of speech: first, untruthfulness; second, divisiveness; third, defaming another's virtue; fourth, meaninglessness. The reverse of these should be known as the four virtues of speech. There are also, briefly, four kinds of an ordinary person's false speech: speaking in reversal of what was seen or not seen. Know that it is likewise so with what was heard or not heard, sensed or not sensed, and known or not known. The reverse of this should be known as the truthful speech of the noble and the wise.

items.title: The Fifth Numeric Category Opens: The Five Aggregates, With and Without Clinging

items.zh: 已說四種佛教所應知處。次說五種。謂有五種諸欲貪品麁重隨逐，流轉雜染所攝行聚。一、所依所緣自性行聚，二、能領納自性行聚，三、能分別言說分位取諸法相自性行聚，四、能作用自性行聚，五、能了別自性行聚。此五相違，當知即是離欲貪品麁重，還滅、清淨所攝自性行聚。
items.en: The four-thing category of what a Buddhist should know has now been explained. Next, the five-thing category. There are five groupings of formations, trailed by the coarse weight of the class of desire and craving, comprised within the defiled class of flux: first, the grouping whose intrinsic nature is [the body's] support and object; second, the grouping whose intrinsic nature is receiving; third, the grouping whose intrinsic nature is discriminating, speaking, and grasping the marks of phenomena according to circumstance; fourth, the grouping whose intrinsic nature is functioning; fifth, the grouping whose intrinsic nature is discerning. The reverse of these five should be known as the grouping whose intrinsic nature is comprised within the pure class of return, free of the coarse weight of the class of desire and craving.

items.title: The Five Sense Pleasures and Four Grades of Longing for Them, and the Five Destinies as Fruit

items.zh: 又有五種受用欲者所愛境界，諸樂欲者常所追求，常所受用；諸背欲者恒正觀察。謂色、聲、香、味、觸。當知此中，依所追求、所尋思、所染著事，有四種愛樂。謂未來所愛樂事，即所追求；過去所愛樂事，即所尋思；現在所愛樂事，即所染著。此復二種。一、所愛樂事，二、從彼所生所愛樂受。又有五種有情所得受愛非愛業果異熟自體。謂天、人、那落迦、傍生、鬼趣。
items.en: There are also five objects loved by those who partake of sensory desire, constantly pursued and constantly enjoyed by those who delight in desire, and constantly, correctly observed by those who have turned away from desire: namely, form, sound, smell, taste, and touch. Know that herein, depending on what is pursued, what is dwelt on in thought, and what is presently defiled by attachment, there are four kinds of delight: what is delighted in for the future is what is pursued; what is delighted in from the past is what is dwelt on in thought; what is delighted in for the present is what is presently attached to — and this last is itself twofold, the delighted-in object itself, and the delighted-in feeling arising from it. There are also five kinds of embodiment that sentient beings receive as the ripened fruit of agreeable or disagreeable karma: the gods, humans, hell-beings, animals, and hungry ghosts.

blocks.text: Today completes the fours and opens the fives with the five aggregates of clinging. One list, four kinds of striving sorted by pleasure and benefit, gives a frank picture of how practice often feels.

A trainee cultivates the higher mind for four reasons. Master Cháng Bǎi notes this reading draws on fascicle 12's four aims of concentration (Day 91). Karma is reduced to four colours: dark, bright, mixed, and neither (Day 63).

Striving may be pleasant but not beneficial, beneficial but not pleasant, both, or neither. Venerable Miào Jìng prefers the second: "beneficial but not pleasant", because it actually succeeds. The third, both pleasant and beneficial, sounds better, but often means seeking pleasures and the Dharma together, and the pleasures win. Most real progress is not comfortable.
Desire, existence, views, and ignorance yoke beings to suffering.

One being can be sorted four ways. By bondage: an ordinary being, a trainee not yet free of desire, a trainee free of desire, and one beyond self-view. By precepts and view (Venerable Miào Jìng: teaching the Dharma here means insight). By who suffers: some harm only themselves, some only others, some both. The *Pīxún jì*'s example of the last: kings who, not content with their realms, lead armies against each other.

Four faults of speech: untruth, divisiveness, defaming virtue, and meaninglessness. Master Cháng Bǎi maps them onto the four verbal misdeeds of Day 57. The four ordinary lies are about the seen, heard, sensed (覺, reflected on by the sixth consciousness), and known.

subs.head: The fives: aggregates with and without clinging

blocks.text: The fives open with the **five aggregates**, with and without clinging. Venerable Miào Jìng: "craving" here includes the subtle craving of the form and formless realms, not only sense desire. Perception, Master Cháng Bǎi notes, "discriminates by names and can speak"; speech follows perception.

The five sense pleasures and four grades of longing for them. Present attachment has two sides. Master Cháng Bǎi: "Loving a rice dumpling is attachment to the object; loving the pleasure of eating it is attachment to the feeling." Practice can address either: seeing the object as impermanent, or seeing the feeling as suffering.

quiz.q: For the four means by which a trainee cultivates the higher mind, what does Master Cháng Bǎi say his reading is based on, and whom does it differ from?
options: on the Yiyan commentary, fascicle 6, and the four cultivations of concentration in fascicle 12 — differing from the Pixunji and Venerable Miào Jìng
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this reading draws on the *Yiyan*, fascicle 6, and the four cultivations of concentration in fascicle 12, "differing from the *Pixunji* and from Venerable Miào Jìng." The *Pixunji* reads the four means as the four immeasurables.

quiz.q: Among the four kinds of striving, which does Venerable Miào Jìng consider more ideal, and what does the reading note say?
options: he says all four are equal
he favours the second, beneficial but not pleasant, as it succeeds; the third seeks both pleasures and Dharma, each undermining the other; the note calls the third ideal
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Of these four, the second is rather more ideal — beneficial but not pleasant — because it can succeed." The third mixes sensual pursuit with Dharma, which undermine each other. The note's "ideal case" for the third conflicts.

quiz.q: Which four kinds of persons, per the treatise, comprehend all persons?
options: the ordinary being, the trainee not free of desire, the trainee free of desire, and the adept beyond self-view
quiz.why: "First, the ordinary being; second, the trainee not yet free of desire; third, the trainee already free of desire; fourth, the adept who has entirely transcended the view of a substantial self." Master Cháng Bǎi: the arhat has cut both conceptual and innate self-grasping.

quiz.q: Kings "impose suffering on both self and others." How does the Pixunji explain this?
options: not content with their own realm, kings lead armies against each other, thus imposing suffering on both
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: kings, not content with their own capitals and villages, lead armies against one another, thus burdening both self and others with suffering and producing demerit. Venerable Miào Jìng: with so much land and wealth, they still invade others.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi map the four faults of speech onto the four verbal misdeeds?
options: untruth is lying, divisiveness is divisive speech, defaming virtue is harsh speech, meaninglessness is frivolous talk
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: divisiveness is divisive speech that breaks others' bonds, and one's own household will later be broken too; defaming virtue is harsh speech. Venerable Miào Jìng: meaningless speech is careless talk that makes others careless.

quiz.q: Which aggregate is the third grouping — "discriminating, speaking, and grasping the marks of phenomena" — per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: perception — it discriminates by names and speaks; speech follows perception
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: perception discriminates by names and can speak — names precede perception, perception precedes speech; the various states of discriminating and speaking are its circumstantial distinctions. The five groupings are form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness.

quiz.q: The present attachment is twofold — the object and the feeling it produces. What image does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: loving the rice dumpling is attachment to the object; loving the pleasure of eating it is attachment to feeling
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "One is attachment to the object, one is attachment to the feeling. Loving a rice dumpling is attachment to the object; loving the pleasant feeling of eating it is attachment to feeling." The first three are by time; the fourth by feeling.
